subject: QBR: capacity model & cost tradeoffs for GPU fleet
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: QBR: capacity model & cost tradeoffs for GPU fleet

Team —

As we lock slides for the Nov QBR I want a concise annex we can hand leadership that shows:
  - near-term GPU spend forecast (monthly) and utilization by pool,
  - unit economics sensitivity to batching and prefix/KV caching,
  - breakpoints for when Reserved (Dedicated) capacity vs. on-demand makes sense (3/6/12 month horizons).

I started a model (attached) with baseline assumptions — please review the numbers in the model tab and push updates to the file: qbr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx. Key prompts below:
  1) Marcus — can you update pool-level utilization and realistic saturation points for each shard type (A100-80GB, H100-80GB, and the mixed-precision T4 pool)? Include the current eviction/backpressure thresholds.
  2) Hannah — run the batching/caching sim (attached CSV) with the latest request mix (chat vs single-turn long-context generation) and surface the marginal cost per 1M tokens at the 50/70/90 percentile latency constraints.
  3) Grace — finance will want to see committed vs on-demand TCO — can you produce a 12-month spend/commitment chart and point out when a 6-mo reservation yields >12% savings under current utilization forecasts?

I plan to include a short one-slide recommendation for the execs: either (A) modest Dedicated commit for H100-heavy pools + aggressive KV caching rollout, or (B) keep on-demand but fund an ops sprint to improve batching heuristics. I need the numbers to defend either path.

Thanks — please treat this as high priority (QBR is in two weeks).

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Infrastructure & Platform
Redwood Inference

> 
> As we lock slides for the Nov QBR I want a concise annex we can hand leadership that shows...

Attached: gpu_utilization_by_pool.png — snapshot of last 90 days by pool. Quick notes from my side:
  - Current steady-state utilization: H100 pool 62% (spiky to 88% peak during EMEA morning), A100 pool 54%, mixed-precision T4 pool 41%.
  - Eviction/backpressure: H100 pool starts tail latency degradation after sustained >75% active batch occupancy for >12 minutes.
  - Average batching factor (tokens per inference call aggregated) across chat workloads: 1.8x overall; with stronger prefix caching we expect 2.4–3.0x on historical request patterns.

Inputs I added to the spreadsheet:
  - realistic headroom buffer to maintain 99th pct latency SLO: +12% capacity buffer for H100 and +18% for A100.
  - A scenario tab: "6-mo commit" where we assume a 20% discount on committed H100 hours; savings are highly sensitive to utilization — you only break even if sustained utilization >70% over 6 months.

Questions for slides and ask items:
  - Do we want to recommend a targeted reserved commit for a single model family (H100) to protect high-throughput supervised fine-tuning and retrieval-heavy chat?
  - If we recommend reserved capacity, what’s the maximum dollars the Finance lead will sign off on pre-approval? (Grace)

I updated the filename in Drive to indicate the new utilization capture.

—Marcus

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR: capacity model & cost tradeoffs for GPU fleet

Thanks — I ran the batching vs latency sim and pushed results into the simulation tab. Summary:
  - Baseline (no prefix/KV caching, conservative batching): marginal cost = $28.6 per 1M tokens at median latency 220ms.
  - With prefix KV caching (50% cache hit assumed for chat histories): marginal cost drops to $19.4 per 1M tokens at median latency 240ms (cache bookkeeping adds small overhead).
  - With improved batching heuristics (opportunistic, up to 3x batching when queueing allows): marginal cost = $12.9 per 1M tokens but 95th pct latency increases by ~85ms.

I also included a short sensitivity table: if model size grows (2x context), batching benefits shrink ~35% and caching benefits grow (higher repetition in prompts). The CSV shows per-scenario token counts and simulated RPC efficiency.

Recommendation: Prioritize prefix/KV caching rollout in next sprint (we can get big dollars back for modest engineering effort), and pair that with a conservative 3-month Dedicated pilot on H100 to validate both utilization and discount assumptions.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Performance Engineering
Redwood Inference

Team —

I pulled together a 12-mo committed vs on-demand cashflow chart (see the spreadsheet). High level:
  - A 6-mo commitment on H100 at 20% discount reduces expected spend by ~14% if utilization is 72%+. Lower utilization flips the ROI negative.
  - Operational risk: if utilization drops quickly (customer churn, model changes) we carry committed spend — recommend a canary approach: commit to 30% of projected H100 steady-state footprint for 3 months, re-evaluate.

Also copied Finance contact from Acme (finance_ops@acme.ai) — they wanted to flag the importance of documenting utilization assumptions when we propose the commit for exec approval.

Great work, everyone — this is exactly the level of granular decision support I wanted. Quick summary to land with Execs Friday: 
  1) Recommendation: a conservative pilot (3 months, 30% of H100 footprint) + immediate rollout of prefix/KV caching and a small ops sprint for batching heuristics.
  2) Expected financial outcome: ~8–12% expected monthly spend reduction if pilot utilization hits 70%+; best-case (with batching improvements) shows >20% savings.
  3) Risks and mitigations: committed dollars if utilization drops (mitigate via convertible credit and ability to reassign capacity to internal burst workloads), potential 95th pct latency regressions with aggressive batching (mitigate via A/B rollout and real-time SLO throttles).

Grace — please include the pilot pre-approval ask (not to exceed $420k cap) on the QBR approval slide. Marcus/Hannah — include a one-slide technical appendix on queueing thresholds and the caching rollout plan. Eva — appreciate the partner terms, please include the convertible credit term in the appendix.

I'll collate final slide and annex tomorrow morning and circulate the packet.

—Jonas
